scope: Proposition 8.1 (Odd-degree splitting) of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let p be prime, L = ⌈log2 p⌉, and B = 20 + (n + 1)(L + 1). Suppose that p > B200000 and that F ∈ Fp[X] is monic, square-free, totally split, and of odd degree 3 ≤ N ≤ n. Choose an odd prime q | N. Suppose that the following data are supplied explicitly: • a field K/Fp of degree at most q − 1; • a primitive q-th root of unity ζ ∈ K; • an element ωK ∈ K∗ of order qvq(|K|−1). There is a deterministic algorithm, denoted by OddSplit, that returns a nontrivial proper monic divisor of F over Fp in a number of bit operations bounded by a fixed polynomial in B.
